mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or enterprise registration authority in the foreign parent company's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention route: notarize if required, apply for an Apostille from the Designated Competent Authority of the issuing jurisdiction, then prepare a sworn Chinese translation in China; no PRC consular legalization. Non-member route: notarize, authenticate through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize through the Consular Section of the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that jurisdiction, and prepare a sworn Chinese translation. The apostille and consular routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or equivalent competent authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention route: secure an Apostille from the Designated Competent Authority of the issuing state, followed by sworn Chinese translation; no consular legalization. Non-member route: secure authentication by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalization by the Consular Section of the PRC Embassy/Consulate in that state, followed by sworn Chinese translation. These routes are alternative and exclusive; do not chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney approving the establishment of the WFOE and appointing the legal representative and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent company and authorized signatories, evidenced by notarial minutes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Because this is a private document, it must first be notarized by a competent notary in the origin jurisdiction. If the origin jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention Contracting Party, the notarized document then receives an Apostille from the designated competent authority, and a sworn Chinese translation is prepared; no PRC Embassy legalization. If the origin jurisdiction is not a Contracting Party, the notarized document is authenticated by the local foreign ministry and then legalized by the PRC Embassy/Consulate, followed by a sworn Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives; never apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document) of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry, registered agent, or notary public holding the authorized certified copy of the constitutional document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention route: certified copy is notarized and apostilled by the origin state's Designated Competent Authority, then translated by a sworn translator into Chinese; no consular step. Non-member route: certified copy is notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalized by the PRC Embassy/Consulate, and then translated; the two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Bank Reference Letter for the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate account bank of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: the bank letter is notarized unless the bank itself is authorized to affix an apostille, then affixed with an Apostille by the origin state's Designated Competent Authority, and translated into Chinese; no PRC consular legalization. Consular route: the bank letter is notarized, authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalized by the PRC Embassy/Consulate, and translated into Chinese. Use only one route depending on the origin state; never chain the two.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to any incorporation filing, all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons owning at least 25% of equity or controlling the entity), and material counterparties must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Sectoral Sanctions Identification Lists, the PRC Ministry of Public Security terrorist list, and domestic PBOC AML/CFT blacklists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP), their family members and close associates; if a PEP is identified, senior management approval and enhanced transaction monitoring must be documented. Screening must be refreshed immediately before notarization and again before bank account opening, and all findings and alerts must be escalated in writing to the AML compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Application and Reservation System, accessed through provincial Market Regulation Bureau online service portals and the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory company names must use simplified Chinese characters and adhere to the four-tier naming order: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or operating characteristics plus legal form. An English name is not the legal name of a WFOE; any English name used commercially is merely a transliteration or auxiliary mark and should correspond to the pinyin of the Chinese name. Arabic numerals, Latin letters, punctuation and symbols are generally disallowed unless the registry grants an exemption. Names containing China, International, National, or Central tokens are subject to elevated approval thresholds and stricter registered capital or business-scope requirements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a reconsideration request with the same

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Amendment), Articles 23-30, 36-40, 46-49, 61-66; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 4, 6, 12, 14; Regulations on the Administration of Foreign Investment in China (State Council Decree No. 723), Articles 5-9
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Enterprise Registration Bureau, and its local counterpart (e.g., Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation) for the registered office jurisdiction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise (Form A) together with the Articles of Association and the Certificate of Incorporation (Business License) issued by SAMR
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE under Chinese law; however, the registered capital must be fully subscribed within the time limit specified in the Articles of Association (typically 30 years from incorporation). The capital may be contributed in cash or in-kind, and must be deposited into a designated bank account in China. No escrow or blocked account requirement applies, but the capital must be verifiable and used for legitimate business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (THE 'COMPANY') ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE] AT [PLACE]. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the laws of the People's Republic of China on [DATE], with registration number [REG. NO.]; and WHEREAS, the Board of Directors (the 'Board') is authorized to manage the affairs of the Company pursuant to the Articles of Association; and WHEREAS, the Board deems it necessary to adopt resolutions regarding the subscription of share capital, the appointment of statutory officers, the adoption of a registered office, and the authorization of banking arrangements. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby confirms that the registered capital of the Company is [AMOUNT] RMB, divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares of [PAR VALUE] RMB each. The sole shareholder, [SHAREHOLDER NAME], has subscribed to all such shares and has agreed to contribute the full amount in accordance with the payment schedule set forth in the Articles of Association. The Board acknowledges receipt of the capital contribution certificate and directs the Company's legal counsel to file the necessary capital verification report with the relevant authorities. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of a corporate bank account with [BANK NAME], [BRANCH], and designates the following individuals as authorized signatories: [NAME], [TITLE], and [NAME], [TITLE], each of whom shall have the power to sign, endorse, and execute all banking documents, including but not limited to checks, wire transfers, and loan agreements, subject to the dual-signature requirement for any transaction exceeding RMB [AMOUNT]. The Board further authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to manage the account and to provide the bank with any necessary corporate documents. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board hereby adopts the registered office of the Company at [FULL ADDRESS], [CITY], [PROVINCE], China, as the legal address for all official communications and service of process. The Company shall maintain its corporate records and statutory registers at this address, and shall notify the SAMR of any change within 30 days. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following individuals to the following statutory positions: [NAME] as Chairman of the Board and Legal Representative; [NAME] as General Manager (Chief Executive Officer); [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer; and [NAME] as Supervisor. Each appointee shall serve until their successor is duly elected or until their earlier resignation, removal, or disqualification. The Legal Representative is authorized to execute all documents on behalf of the Company, including contracts, tax filings, and regulatory submissions. 5. GENERAL: The Board authorizes the officers and legal counsel to take all necessary actions to implement these resolutions, including the preparation and filing of any required documents with the State Administration for Market Regulation, the tax authorities, and other regulatory bodies. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of the Board. ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY by the Board on the date first written above. /s/ [CHAIRMAN] /s/ [SECRETARY]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Enterprise Name Registration Online Portal (https://www.samr.gov.cn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for pre-approval of the proposed company name (e.g., 'Shanghai [Brand] Education Technology Co., Ltd.') through the SAMR online system. The name must comply with the Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration (2018) and must not conflict with existing trademarks or registered entities. Provide the intended business scope and the legal structure (WFOE). The system will issue a Name Pre-Approval Notice (valid for 6 months) upon successful review. Ensure that the name includes the industry descriptor 'Education Technology' or 'Software' to align with the ISIC 6201 scope. If the name is rejected, revise and resubmit within 5 working days.
required_dossiers: Identification of the sole shareholder (passport or corporate registration certificate)
Power of attorney for the local agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or non-compliance, file an administrative reconsideration with the SAMR within 15 days of the rejection notice, or submit a revised name application. The remedy typically involves providing additional evidence of distinctiveness or adjusting the name structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office in the jurisdiction of the shareholder (if foreign) and the local SAMR office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association, the Shareholder's Resolution, and the Application for Registration. The Articles must include the company name, registered address, business scope, registered capital, shareholder details, board composition, and governance rules. All documents must be in Chinese; if the shareholder is a foreign entity, the documents must be notarized by a notary public in the shareholder's home country and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate (or apostilled if the country is a party to the Hague Convention). Additionally, the shareholder's certificate of incorporation and passport copies must be notarized. Submit the notarized documents to the local SAMR office for preliminary review. The SAMR will verify the completeness and legality of the documents. Any deficiencies must be corrected within 10 working days.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized shareholder identification (passport or corporate registration)
Articles of Association (original, signed by all shareholders)
Lease agreement for the registered office (or property ownership certificate)
Power of attorney for the local agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR issues a query or suspension, the applicant must provide supplementary documents or clarifications within 15 days. If the issue is substantive (e.g., illegal business scope), the applicant may amend the Articles and resubmit. If the SAMR rejects the application, an administrative appeal can be filed with the higher-level SAMR within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local SAMR Enterprise Registration Window (e.g., Shanghai Municipal Administration for Market Regulation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete application package, including the notarized documents, the name pre-approval notice, the lease agreement, and the application form, to the local SAMR office. The application must be filed in person or through the online portal. Pay the official filing fee (approximately RMB 1,000, equivalent to USD 150) via bank transfer or online payment. The SAMR will review the application for compliance with the Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law. The review typically takes 5-10 working days. Upon approval, the SAMR will issue the Business License (营业执照) with a unified social credit code. The license will specify the company's legal representative, registered capital, and business scope.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the legal representative and supervisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, the SAMR must provide a written reason. The applicant may correct the deficiencies and resubmit within 30 days. If the rejection is based on substantive legal grounds, the applicant may appeal to the administrative review committee or file a lawsuit in the People's Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Bureau, Public Security Bureau (for company seal), Social Insurance Bureau, and the local Statistics Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business License, the company must complete the following within 30 days: (1) Register with the tax authority for a tax identification number and obtain the tax registration certificate (now integrated into the business license); (2) Apply for the company seal (official seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal) at the Public Security Bureau; (3) Register with the Social Insurance Bureau for employee social insurance; (4) Register with the Statistics Bureau for statistical reporting. Additionally, the company must open a corporate bank account and deposit the registered capital (if any) within the specified period. The company must also file the Articles of Association with the local commerce department (if required) and obtain the Foreign Investment Certificate (now replaced by the Foreign Investment Information Report).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any registration is delayed, the company may be subject to fines. To cure, submit the required documents as soon as possible and pay any late fees. For tax registration, the company can apply for an extension if there are extenuating circumstances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) for ICP licensing, and the National Copyright Administration for software copyright registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an EdTech software company, the following licenses are typically required: (1) Internet Content Provider (ICP) license (if the company operates a website or mobile app with user-facing content) – apply to the MIIT or its provincial branch; (2) Software copyright registration with the National Copyright Administration to protect the proprietary software; (3) If the company processes personal data, it must comply with the Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) and may need to conduct a data protection impact assessment. Additionally, if the company offers online education services, it may need to obtain an approval from the Ministry of Education (MOE) for online education platforms, depending on the nature of the content. The company must also register with the local cyberspace administration for any online content. These licenses are not required for pure software development without user-facing services, but for a subscription-based EdTech platform, they are mandatory.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ICP license is denied, the company can appeal to the MIIT within 60 days. For MOE approval, the company may need to adjust its business model to comply with regulations. If the company operates without the required licenses, it may be subject to fines and shutdown orders. The remedy is to obtain the licenses before commencing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – The business scope is purely digital (ISIC 6201 – Computer programming, consultancy and related activities) and does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – No industrial operating license is required for a software development and EdTech subscription service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – The Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) does not require an EIA for digital service providers.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – The activity does not fall under any category listed in the Environmental Impact Assessment Classification List (2021).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation occurs in a software development environment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – The company operates in a standard office environment; however, the office must comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (2019) and obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire department. The company must also ensure workplace safety per the Occupational Health and Safety Law, but no special industrial clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, with electronic filing through the STA-administered National Electronic Tax Office (ETax) online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Chinese WFOE, the statutory taxpayer identity is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) automatically issued and shared by the State Administration for Market Regulation with the STA under the multi-license integration system. This USCC functions as the TIN and VAT registration number; no separate TIN procurement application is needed for the locally incorporated entity. A foreign non-resident enterprise with no Chinese establishment must complete non-resident enterprise tax registration through the ETax non-resident taxpayer module before earning income from China source, providing its home-country registration certificate, foreign board-and-director details, address, contract meeting the source-of-income rule, and designated bank relationship. The competent tax authority then records a non-resident registration code for withholding and indirect-tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections for entity classification; a WFOE is mandatorily a Chinese resident enterprise. The only relevant commercial election is that a small-scale VAT taxpayer may voluntarily be registered as a general VAT taxpayer upon satisfying accounting and compliance conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for initial VAT registration; the WFOE is VAT-registered from incorporation. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer classification is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000. The WFOE's EdTech subscription service is an information technology / educational service subject to the 6% VAT rate for domestic supplies, while the 13% statutory headline rate applies to goods sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued only through the STA electronic invoice system controlled by Golden Tax Phase IV. Fully digitalized electronic invoices carry STA-assigned digital fingerprints, and issuance data is transmitted in near-real-time to the STA clearance platform through the National Electronic Tax Office APIs. The anti-fraud mandate requires three-way matching among invoice, export/customs event, and foreign exchange receipt for zero-rated exports; cross-border app-store sales must be reconciliable to Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement statements, with e-invoices issued to overseas B2B buyers or aggregate reporting accepted for foreign B2C consumers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of goods from the PRC customs territory qualifies for 0% VAT upon verified customs departure and foreign exchange receipt. For the WFOE's digital EdTech language-learning services, 0% VAT applies to qualifying cross-border services delivered to foreign non-resident users and consumed entirely outside China; eligibility requires clear evidence of the non-resident customer, offshore consumption, foreign payment remittance, and no substantial domestic user base or local consumption in China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Goods Customs Declaration captured electronically in the China Customs export declaration system
Original bill of lading or air waybill evidencing physical exit of merchandise from China
Export commercial invoice and packing list
Bank inward remittance advice or State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) trade-monitoring record evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency

For digital EdTech subscription sales: non-resident customer agreement, IP/geolocation evidence, app-store settlement reports from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, and cross-border foreign-currency payment receipts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs jointly mine Golden Tax Phase IV data to verify export declarations, invoice issuance, foreign exchange collection, and payment settlement. A zero-rating claim that fails audit triggers retrospective clawback of the VAT refund or zero-rating benefit plus additional VAT liability, a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the tax amount under the PRC Law on Tax Collection and Administration. Intentional fabrication of exports, forged bills of lading, or fictitious app-store receipts is referred to the criminal courts under the PRC Criminal Law, where fraudulent export refunds can attract imprisonment up to life; fraudulent assessments are not statute-barred, while ordinary documentation defects remain open for retrospective reassessment for up to five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a bifurcated convertibility framework. Current account transactions, including software licensing fees, EdTech subscription commissions, and payments for services, are largely convertible after the settlement bank completes a real-need authenticity review of contract, invoice, tax payment, and SAFE service trade registration records. Capital account items are not freely convertible by ministerial decree: each equity injection, shareholder loan, or liquidation remittance requires a SAFE foreign exchange registration, a dedicated foreign exchange capital account, and actual-use verification. The old mandatory export surrender system has been replaced by a retention-and-settle model: export proceeds must be repatriated through a designated bank and may be held or voluntarily converted into RMB; there is no fixed statutory conversion rate for ordinary software and service exports. Profit repatriation hurdles remain material: an audited statutory financial report, proper dividend resolution, verified cumulative distributable profits, corporate income tax and withholding tax clearance, SAFE capital project reporting, and bank-level ultimate beneficial ownership and sanctions clearance are all required before the dividend is wired out. EdTech firms must further separate Apple and Google billing receipts as cross-border service trade claims and maintain matching platform settlements and royalty calculations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For physical goods exports, proceeds must be repatriated to a designated foreign exchange account within 180 calendar days after the export customs declaration date and matched by the bank in the SAFE trade monitoring system; no uniform mandatory conversion ratio is imposed at the national level. For EdTech cross-border service exports, no customs declaration clock applies; instead, the bank must match each Apple/Google consolidated payout to the underlying service invoices, and any receivable still unpaid 90 days beyond the referenced invoice due date triggers a SAFE service trade authenticity review. The WFOE may retain foreign currency or voluntarily sell it to a domestic bank at the prevailing market rate, although a bank may require an explanation for unusually large retained export balances.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary liquidity rail. Domestic corporate RMB and foreign exchange current and capital account services are reserved for licensed Chinese banks and cannot be provided by offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex unless those EMIs hold a PBOC and SAFE payment institution license and operate through a Chinese domestic bank partner. For a WFOE requiring statutory capital injection and SAFE registration, only a Chinese bank can maintain the regulated capital account records; an EMI can act only as a supplementary collection conduit for low-value international card payments, and even then it must comply with the PBOC non-bank payment institution rules, which currently limit currency conversion and require a Chinese custodian bank. The practical viability is Low for primary treasury and Medium only for ancillary e-commerce disbursements if a licensed domestic partner is used.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a WFOE first corporate account opening, Chinese banks generally require the statutory legal representative or a senior authorised signatory to appear physically at a branch for a face-to-face KYC interview and identity verification; a remote consular proxy opening is not a standard right and every bank must approve it under its internal proxy account opening procedure with notarised power of attorney plus Chinese embassy/consulate legalisation and Chinese-language translation. Even where remote video verification is accepted in pilot cities, the local branch manager must still verify the original business license, articles of association, foreign investment information report, SAFE registration, company chop, financial officer identity, and the ultimate beneficial owners holding more than 25%, and final approval may require a second in-person visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque shareholder chain above the WFOE using trusts, foundations, or non-public holding companies prevents the identification of natural persons controlling the EdTech parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group holding structure chart; certificate of incorporation and memorandum; registers of members and directors; trust deed and protector approval; notarised passports and residential proof of each UBO; source-of-wealth statement; three-year audited financial statements of the direct parent; a reference letter from a reputable correspondent bank; and Chinese notarised translations of all documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hits, or common names in the beneficial ownership list, trigger enhanced due diligence and may cause automatic account refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed database screening results from Dow Jones, World-Check, or Refinitiv; negative news analysis; official police and court clearance certificates; evidence of address and employment history; a regulatory letter of good standing from the foreign business registry; and a sworn affidavit explaining each hit and disproving connection to corruption, weapons proliferation, human trafficking, or restricted jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Predicted payment flow disconnect because the WFOE receives Apple and Google App Store settlements from offshore platforms without matching software licensing or content royalty contracts, suggesting fake digital subscriptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple and Google developer agreements; merchant payout statements; app store listing pages; end-user license agreement; privacy policy; a fair-value transfer pricing study for the technology and course-content licence; invoices from the controlling entity; tax withholding registration; and a reconciliation model proving platform settlement receipts match reported revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity capital is immediately converted and paid to connected companies without operating payroll, supplier, or leasing evidence, indicating capital account proceeds being diverted or round-tripped.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE registered use-of-funds schedule; lease and office agreements; supplier and payroll contracts; board-approved budget and treasury policy; cash-flow forecast; VAT and corporate income tax filings; customs declarations where relevant; and a domestic bank undertaking letter for each counterparty if the transfer exceeds the suspicious transaction threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first complete SAFE foreign-investment information registration and open a foreign exchange capital account. The non-resident shareholder should wire capital through SWIFT MT103 to that account; the remitter name and bank account must exactly match the registered shareholder, and the reference field should contain the SAFE foreign exchange registration number and the Chinese balance-of-payments purpose code for equity capital from direct investment. After receipt, the bank reports the transaction into the SAFE capital project information system, and any conversion into RMB is done on a real-need basis after the bank verifies the intended use of funds; a Chinese certified public accountant should then perform capital verification and issue a report for registration and subsequent remittance compliance. The resulting RMB amount must be credited into the domestic basic settlement account and spent only on the WFOE operating scope; prohibited uses include equity investment, real estate purchase outside pilot rules, wealth management, and speculative securities transactions. For larger receipts the bank may also require a board resolution, share subscription price evidence, and a source-of-funds confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EdTech operating payments, use SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wire transfers of royalties, software licensing, teacher-side payments, cloud service fees, and marketing expenses, supported by contract, invoice, tax voucher, and tax withholding proof; use clearing rails such as China International Payment System (CIPS) when the beneficiary accepts cross-border RMB. For physical goods such as course accessories or hardware imports, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are available through the issuing Chinese bank, but software-heavy EdTech flows should rely primarily on MT103 and CIPS. Every outgoing payment must also be integrated with SAFE trade in services reporting and the bank AML transaction monitoring system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD, CNY/EUR, and CNY/HKD deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts against genuine future CNY or FX cash flows, supported by underlying contracts or forecast exposure, entered under a master agreement with the settlement bank and subject to margin collateral requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards are not permitted for the onshore WFOE as its own hedge where domestic CNY is deliverable; NDFs are generally restricted to offshore counterparties without an onshore CNY funding base, and any group-level NDF strategy must be structured outside the WFOE balance sheet.

Cross-currency swaps for one to five year capital and dividend exposures may be used only for documented principal, interest, or dividend cash-flow hedging of the WFOE equity capital or shareholder loans, and must comply with SAFE real-demand derivatives principle; speculative naked positions are prohibited and the bank will demand ISDA and credit support annex documentation plus SAFE reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report (Annual Publication through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year for the preceding financial year ended 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the report is not published by 30 June, SAMR places the WFOE on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; correction within 3 years removes the listing, but continuous non-compliance for 3 years leads to inclusion on the List of Seriously Illegal and Dishonest Market Entities, disqualification of the legal representative and responsible executives from serving as directors or senior managers for 3 years, enhanced credit supervision, and potential administrative fines for false or late reporting local SAMR enforcement rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR through the integrated NECIPS annual reporting portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit, or submission of false annual foreign investment information, triggers an order to correct within 20 working days; failure to correct is penalized under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures with a fine of up to RMB 200,000, and the default is published as a credit impairment affecting future foreign-exchange, financing and procurement channels.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement and Payment (CIT annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local competent tax authority of the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing and final settlement must be completed by 31 May after the end of the tax year; quarterly prepayments are due during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing allows the tax authority to order filing within a prescribed period and impose a penalty of RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; any unpaid tax accrues overdue surcharge of 0.05% per day of the unpaid amount from the statutory due date; deliberate or aggravated under-declaration may be penalized at 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, with enforced levy, bank account freeze, downgrade of taxpayer credit rating and restriction of invoice services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Direct Investment Stock and Interest Information Registration (FDI equity annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the annual direct-investment information registration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June each year for the equity and interest balances outstanding at 31 December of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the FDI stock and interest registration results in suspension of foreign-exchange capital account procedures, denial of foreign-exchange settlement and payment, restriction on subsequent cross-border equity transfers and dividend remittances, and inclusion in SAFE credit supervision records; intentional violations may additionally attract warnings and fines under the Regulations on Administration of Foreign Exchange depending on the circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Information Annual Verification and 30-Day Change Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR market entity registration system and the People's Bank of China beneficial-owner information management framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days from the date of change; standing beneficial-owner information must be reconfirmed during the annual enterprise report cycle between 1 January and 30 June each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, omitted or false beneficial-owner reporting exposes the WFOE to an order to correct within a prescribed deadline and, if not corrected, fines of up to RMB 100,000 on the entity and up to RMB 10,000 on directly responsible personnel under the Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures; continued non-compliance also triggers enhanced anti-money-laundering supervision and market-entity credit impairment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit of Financial Statements by a Licensed PRC CPA Firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a registry filing; audited financial statements and audit report must be retained for inspection by SAMR, STA and SAFE and used to support the annual CIT settlement, foreign investment information report and FDI registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit report must be dated sufficiently early to support the annual CIT settlement due by 31 May and the annual report cycle due by 30 June each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit violates Article 164 of the PRC Company Law, exposes the WFOE to administrative rectification orders, refusal of tax loss carry-forwards and tax incentives, rejection or impairment of the enterprise annual report, loss of clean foreign-exchange registration status, and liability of the company and responsible officers if unaudited financial statements are submitted to any authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC Company Law Article 164 imposes a statutory audit on every limited liability company, including a WFOE, irrespective of balance-sheet total, annual turnover or headcount; there is no small-company exemption. The audit mandate therefore applies even if the WFOE has zero revenue, zero employees, or a balance sheet below any commercial threshold. The audit must be performed by a licensed PRC accounting firm under the Chinese Standards on Auditing (CSA), and the audited financial statements must be prepared under PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/Chinese GAAP).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/Chinese GAAP), substantially converged with IFRS; small qualifying enterprises may apply the Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises (EAS), but a WFOE engaged in foreign investment reporting or consolidated by a foreign parent must generally apply full ASBE for domestic statutory purposes; IFRS as issued by the IASB is not a standalone statutory reporting basis for a PRC WFOE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PRC does not maintain an EU-style standalone annual UBO return. Under the Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures and the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, the WFOE must identify its beneficial owners, maintain internal records, report initial beneficial-owner information, file any subsequent change with SAMR within 30 days of the change, and reconfirm the standing data during the annual enterprise report cycle between 1 January and 30 June. Any shareholding transfer that changes members or beneficial owners also triggers a SAMR alteration registration within 30 days; the statutory 30-day window cannot be postponed to the end of the accounting year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Shareholders) including name, capital contribution, share certificate details and registration dates
Register of Directors, Executive Officers, Supervisors and Legal Representative
Register of Charges, Pledges and Mortgages including equity pledges and security interests in company assets
Minute Book containing signed minutes and resolutions of shareholders' general meetings, board meetings and supervisory board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 3,000 per year depending on city and whether the service provider supplies virtual office, mail handling, compliance support and SAMR/SAFE annual filing assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 20,000 per year depending on the scale of assets, turnover, intercompany balances, headcount, transaction complexity and the tier of the licensed CPA firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% statutory headline rate under Article 4 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potentially reduced effective rates are available: 15% for a recognized High and New Technology Enterprise; for a certified software enterprise, a two-year exemption followed by three years at half rate (12.5% effective) from the first profit-making year; a 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; and for qualifying technology transfer income an exemption up to RMB 5 million with a 50% reduction on the excess. Certain free-zone or key-technology local incentives may further lower the effective rate. There is no separate patent-box regime outside these technology and software measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Class A) - Form A200000 and its supplementary schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal. Key schedules include the A105080 depreciation and amortization schedule, A107012 R&D additional deduction schedule, A107010 preferential tax treatment schedule, and G100000 related-party transaction reporting schedule.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing, with quarterly provisional EIT prepayments during the year; the annual return is the final settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed and the final balance paid within five months of the fiscal year-end, meaning no later than 31 May for a calendar-year WFOE. Quarterly provisional prepayments are due within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from online language-learning subscriptions, digital tutoring software licenses, and ancillary EdTech services, stated VAT-exclusive under PRC Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross customer consideration collected through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, recording platform commissions as selling expenses rather than netting them. Reconcile Box 1 to platform settlement statements and do not route subscription revenue to an overseas affiliate absent an arm's length transfer-pricing arrangement. Even if customers are located abroad, the WFOE, being a Chinese resident enterprise, must report worldwide income, and China-source revenue rules may still apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs include employee compensation, server hosting, content development, teacher and tutor delivery costs, marketing, Apple and Google platform commissions, depreciation, royalties, technology service fees, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalty and service fees paid to non-resident related parties are deductible only if supported by written contracts, actual service performance, economic substance, and arm's length pricing. If the foreign recipient is a shell entity or the fee exceeds arm's length, the tax authority will add back the excessive portion. Keep evidence of withholding at source, VAT calculation, and DTA relief documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before income tax calculated under the PRC Accounting Standards (CAS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all group allocation charges, intercompany loan interest, and IP licensing fees are backed by books and records. For a thin-capitalised WFOE, related-party interest deductions are limited by the debt-to-equity ratio (2:1 for non-financial enterprises) and must be at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add non-deductible expenses such as entertainment exceeding statutory caps, administrative penalties, illegal invoices, excessive related-party charges, and interest exceeding thin-capitalisation limits. Subtract tax-exempt income including qualifying technology-transfer income and certain government grants.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the R&D additional deduction only for software-development and AI/learning-technology activities actually performed in China. Where transfer-pricing adjustments have been made, record them here and reconcile with Schedule G100000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set-off against current-year taxable income any prior-year tax losses within the statutory carryforward term.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The standard carryforward is five years. If the WFOE qualifies as a High and New Technology Enterprise or a small-to-medium science-technology enterprise, a ten-year loss carryforward may be available. No loss carryforward is permitted for double-counted or transfer-pricing-related amounts previously shifted offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after tax adjustments, loss carryforwards, and preferential deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must not leave Box 6 artificially low by paying excessive management fees or royalty fees to an IP-owning non-resident affiliate with no substance. Tax authorities are authorized to re-determine taxable income on an arm's length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rate applied to taxable income: 25% standard, 15% with valid High and New Technology Enterprise certification, 12.5% effective during the software enterprise three-year half-rate window, or the small-low-profit enterprise effective rate if qualified.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A preferential rate must be evidenced by a certificate valid for the tax year and filed with the tax authority before the annual due date. The rate cannot be self-selected without formal qualification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable rate, reduced by preferential tax reductions and credits, including technology-transfer deductions and any other article-based tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where profit is later distributed to a non-resident shareholder, the 10% dividend withholding tax, or reduced DTA rate, arises separately at the shareholder level and is not an expense of the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid overseas on foreign-source income included in the Chinese tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE may claim a foreign tax credit against Chinese EIT for taxes paid on foreign-source income, capped at the Chinese EIT attributable to that income. Withholding tax suffered on outbound dividends or outbound royalties is a shareholder-level or recipient-level tax and is not creditable in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total provisional EIT instalments paid during the year on a quarter-by-quarter basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the cumulative amount actually remitted. Underpaying quarterly instalments in order to finance an offshore distribution can trigger statutory late-payment interest and administrative penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balancing figure after annual tax payable, prepayments, foreign tax credits, and all other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance must be settled by the annual statutory deadline. If a refund is due, formally apply for refund or set-off. Deliberately balancing to zero through fraudulent invoices or fake intercompany charges is a criminal tax-evasion indicator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all related-party transactions, including cross-border royalty, service, loan, tangible-property, and financial-asset transactions with the foreign parent and affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The schedule must state transaction categories, amounts, transfer-pricing methodologies, the tested party, and contemporaneous documentation. It is mandatory in the annual return for enterprises that have related-party transactions. Failure to file is a separate administrative violation and increases the audit risk of the entire WFOE group.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual filing attracts a penalty under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious cases. Underpaid tax bears late-payment interest of 0.05% per day. Where underpayment results from false invoices, false related-party reporting, or transfer-pricing mispricing, the tax authority may impose a 50% to five times surcharge on the tax evaded. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can lead to imprisonment and fines for responsible officers, and the entity may be publicly blacklisted by the State Taxation Administration.
